source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Fruit flies attacking citrus lay eggs in ripening fruit; the larvae then feed inside the fruit, causing it to rot and drop prematurely, and creating small entry punctures on the rind surface that are often the first visible sign of infestation.

Because fruit fly larvae develop inside otherwise healthy-looking fruit, infested fruit can be missed at a casual glance and only found to be spoiled when opened, which is a particular problem for fruit destined for market where appearance and quality both matter.

Management includes prompt collection and destruction of fallen and infested fruit (to break the fly's breeding cycle), the use of fruit fly traps or bait stations to reduce adult populations, and where practical, bagging individual fruit on the tree during the vulnerable ripening period to physically exclude egg-laying females.
